intro.heading: Pond work for farms, acreages, and larger rural properties
intro.content: Bellhouse handles pond digging when the job is really about land use, drainage, and material movement, not a decorative water feature brochure. That can mean a new farm pond, a pond expansion, sediment removal from an older pond, or reshaping banks and surrounding grades so the area works better long term.
keypoints: New pond excavation and pond enlargement
Bank reshaping, spoil handling, and grade correction
Useful for farm properties, drainage improvement, and larger rural sites

includes.heading: What Bellhouse pond work covers
includes.subheading: Excavation and cleanup work tied to water capacity, drainage, access, and what happens to the removed material.

items.title: New Pond Excavation
items.description: Bellhouse digs new ponds for rural and farm properties where drainage, water storage, land shaping, or habitat improvement are part of the property plan.

items.title: Pond Expansion and Deepening
items.description: We enlarge existing ponds or cut them deeper when more capacity or better function is needed.

items.title: Sediment and Organic Material Removal
items.description: Older ponds can lose depth and function as silt builds up. Bellhouse can remove accumulated material and restore a more workable shape.

items.title: Shoreline and Surrounding Grade Reshaping
items.description: Banks, slopes, and drainage around the pond can be reshaped so the site works better after the excavation is done.

equipment.heading: Equipment used for pond projects
equipment.subheading: Machines suited to excavation, spoil movement, and shaping larger rural properties.

items.title: Excavator
items.description: Used for pond digging, sediment removal, bank shaping, and controlled excavation around water.

items.title: Tri-Axle Dump Trucks
items.description: Bellhouse trucks can haul spoil away or support other material movement when the pond work generates more excavated material than the site can keep.

process.heading: How Bellhouse pond projects are handled
process.subheading: The useful first questions are about site access, drainage, spoil handling, and how the pond is meant to function.

steps.title: Review the property and pond goal
steps.description: Bellhouse looks at access, drainage, water movement, site conditions, and whether the job is a new pond, expansion, or cleanout.

steps.title: Excavate or clean out the pond
steps.description: We dig, deepen, enlarge, or remove accumulated material based on the shape and function the property needs.

steps.title: Manage spoil and shape the banks
steps.description: Removed material is handled according to the site plan, and surrounding grades are shaped so the finished pond ties into the property properly.

steps.title: Leave the area in working condition
steps.description: Bellhouse leaves the pond and surrounding area ready for the next property-use step instead of leaving the site half-shaped and unfinished.

serviceArea.heading: Service Area
serviceArea.content: Bellhouse pond excavation work is strongest across linked service areas where farm, rural, and larger-lot properties need practical digging and cleanout support.

items.question: How deep can you dig a pond?
items.answer: Most ponds are dug 6–12 feet deep, depending on purpose and soil conditions.

items.question: Do you handle wetlands?
items.answer: We can improve drainage and sediment buildup, but regulated wetlands require permits.

items.question: Can you clean an overgrown pond?
items.answer: Yes, we remove sediment, vegetation, and reshape the shoreline.

cta.heading: Need a pond project scoped out?
cta.subheading: Send the property location, the type of pond work, and what the land needs to do better if you want Bellhouse to review fit and next steps.
